pins.title: Walk it like this
items: Take short steps with your weight over your feet
Step flat: the whole sole on the ground
Use trekking poles for balance
Put traction on before the ice, not on it
Watch shaded bends, steps and bridges
pins.sub: No grip to get up and back down safely? Turn around.

pins.kicker: Cold feet on a winter hike?
pins.title: 5 fixes
items: Wool or synthetic socks, never cotton
Leave room in your boots: tight is colder
Change into dry socks at a long break
Add a layer before your core gets cold
Keep snow out of your boots with gaiters
pins.sub: Feet get coldest at breaks, not while you walk.

pins.kicker: Phone won't react to your gloves?
pins.title: Wear a liner
items: Touchscreen gloves work best for quick taps
They fail when wet or loose at the fingertip
Wear a thin touchscreen liner under a warm mitt
Keep the phone in an inside pocket
Keep the screen dry: wet glass misses taps

pins.title: Stay back
pins.sub: Ice can break off without warning, most of all when the sun warms it, and water can still run under the ice at the base. Take the photo from a distance.

pins.kicker: Out of water on a winter hike?
pins.title: Don't eat snow
pins.sub: Your body burns its own heat to melt it, and a handful is barely a sip. Carry enough water and keep it against your back.

pins.kicker: Spare socks wet when you need them?
pins.title: Pack a dry bag
pins.sub: Melting snow soaks through side pockets. Roll your spare socks and gloves into a dry bag, shut it three times and pack it deep inside.

pins.title: Take the cap off
pins.sub: Rubber caps are for pavement and rock. On mud and snow, keep them in your pocket and let the metal tip grip.

pins.title: Watch the shade
items: Shaded slickrock and steps can stay icy all day
Pack traction for your boots
Start early: it gets dark around 5 pm
Pack a warm layer: winter nights often freeze
Check nps.gov for road and trail conditions

pins.title: Plan every month
pins.sub: A printable planner with goals, a hike for each month, the Hike-a-Week Challenge and a mileage tracker to color in.

pins.title: Plan it now
pins.sub: Many popular campgrounds open bookings months ahead. A printable camping planner with meal plans, a car packing list and family checklists.
